clue.text: Buccaneer succeeded in following bad inclination

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: succeeded sits inside the word for bad, so in marks a container here

parts.note: food gone bad is rancid
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
a rake is a slope or incline, as of a stage

explanation.surface: A pirate takes over, driven by some wicked urge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elizabethan seafarer was a privateer to the English but a pirate to the Spanish, which makes 'Buccaneer' fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan sea captain raided Spanish treasure ships, so he is fairly called a pirate.

clue.text: Was agitated Scandinavian arrested by government agent

indicators.note: the government agent holds the Scandinavian, so arrested by means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent, especially of the FBI
a Lapp is a native of Lapland in northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A Nordic traveller grows nervous when an official detains him.
explanation.definitionFit: To flap is to fuss in a state of nervous panic, the past tense matching was agitated.

clue.text: Join crowd, not soft in speech

parts.note: to add is to join one thing to another

indicators.note: the soft letter is dropped from the combined words, so not signals a removal

parts.note: to press is to crowd or throng
P is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Someone tells an audience to mingle boldly, avoiding meekness in a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk given to an audience is an oration or speech.

clue.text: Seconds for good child

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds of time
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: Asking for second helpings is a good kid's habit.
explanation.walkthrough: SPROG is British slang for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang names a young child or baby with this word.

clue.text: Artist showing horse in me standard rising

clue.text: Arch at present protected head of state

indicators.note: the head of state surrounds the phrase for at present, as a guard protects

parts.note: a king is a monarch, a head of state
now means at the present time

explanation.surface: A ruler shields a bridge's curved structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' looks like a noun from architecture; it is the adjective meaning sly or roguish.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means slyly mischievous or teasing, the same as a knowing look.

clue.text: Vast mass in messy album I erase

indicators.note: the mass abbreviation goes inside the jumbled letters
a messy arrangement is a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Someone deletes an enormous pile of untidy photos from a scrapbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' looks like it describes the album; it signals the rearrangement, giving IMEASURABLE before M goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too great to be measured is enormous, so vast is a synonym.

clue.text: Wind low, rose perhaps from the east

parts.note: mean means base or low in character

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, backwards

parts.note: rose is a shade of red, an example marked by perhaps

explanation.surface: A gentle breeze carries a flower's scent in from the eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as moving air; here it is the verb rhyming with find, to twist and turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to follow a twisting course, just as a river does when it bends lazily.

clue.text: Salesman covering criticism

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a roof is a covering over a building

explanation.surface: A travelling seller's shelter attracts complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuke or expression of blame is a form of criticism.

clue.text: A little influence in loud meeting

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: the word for influence sits inside the meeting

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting
action can mean effect or influence on something

explanation.surface: Someone exerts some sway at a noisy gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb meaning by a tiny amount or slightly, just as a little modifies a verb.

clue.text: Clear air

definitions.meaning: clear and explicit, as a stated wish is plain
to air a view is to voice or state it

explanation.definitionFit: An explicit instruction is clear, and to air an opinion is to put it into words.

clue.text: Some chitchat in argument about dessert

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the run is read right to left
only part of the phrase is used, so some marks letters taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A little gossip during a row over the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ATINARG from chitchAT IN ARGument, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian sweet is a grainy water ice served as a dessert.

clue.text: Aspects thought mostly to divide saints

indicators.note: the thought sits between the two saints, splitting them apart

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: Most notions are enough to split holy men apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Different facets or angles of a question are its viewpoints or aspects.

clue.text: Focus of attention in green land

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
to light, as a bird lights on a branch, means to land

explanation.surface: A centre of interest in a verdant country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' is a verb here: to light upon something is to come down on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the centre of public interest is the idiom of being in the stage spotlight.

clue.text: Preserve nearly all filling made after damage

indicators.note: after puts the damage word in front, with the filled word following it

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: the shortened word fills the inside of made

parts.note: made means created, kept as written

indicators.note: nearly drops the last letter

explanation.surface: Keep a nearly finished pie filling made after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb meaning keep; it is the noun for a jam, here the orange kind spread on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, and preserve is the general word for jam.

clue.text: Aim after work in present to get rest

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the word for present

parts.note: to render is to present or give

indicators.note: letters that have been worked on are reshaped, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Aiming to relax once the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after work' reads as time off; here it means once worked over, rearranging AIM into MAI.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest of something is what is left over, the leftover part.

clue.text: Prophet in country bearing endless pain

indicators.note: the country carries the shortened pain inside it

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A seer in some land puts up with ceaseless suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The prophet's book is the last in the Christian Old Testament; 'endless' gives ACH.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the Old Testament prophet whose book closes the Hebrew prophetic writings.

clue.text: Friend back with note enclosed

indicators.note: the note is placed inside the word for back

parts.note: ago means in the past, as in years back
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pal returns carrying a written message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is time past (ten years back), not a direction, and 'note' is musical rather than written.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish borrowing used in English for a pal or companion.

clue.text: Skilled worker is cutting cloth short of time

indicators.note: the little word is cuts into the shortened cloth
the cloth loses the letter for time

parts.note: tartan is a checked woollen cloth from Scotland

explanation.surface: A craftsman trims fabric in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: TARTAN is the checked woollen cloth of Scottish clans; 'short of' leaves ARTAN for 'cutting' to split.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who works with the hands at a trade is a skilled worker.

clue.text: Acting immorally, letting down in turn

indicators.note: in a down entry the first letter is lowered to the bottom of the word

parts.note: sinning is acting immorally

explanation.surface: Behaving badly and disappointing everyone in one's go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting down' sends the S of SINNING to the end. INNINGS is a cricket team's turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a side's period of batting is its turn at the crease.

clue.text: Rubbish covering lake? That is awkward

indicators.note: the rubbish surrounds the lake

parts.note: bosh is nonsense, rubbish
ie is id est, that is

explanation.surface: Is litter hiding a lake? That's a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLSHIE is British slang for uncooperative, from Bolshevik.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stroppy and uncooperative, as the slang word means, is to be awkward.

clue.text: Energy a number consumed

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A quantity of power used up.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been eaten has been used up, swallowed and consumed.

clue.text: Aerial, unusually neat and new, not available

indicators.note: unusually means arranged out of the usual order

explanation.surface: A tidy new radio receiver is out of stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges NEAT and N into ANTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod or wire for receiving radio signals is an aerial in British English.

clue.text: Passage in church right behind cross in eastern part

indicators.note: the cross, church and right go inside the other two
behind places church and right after the cross

parts.note: X is a cross shape
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A corridor in a church lies to the right, beyond a crucifix in the east end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a church corridor; it is a quoted extract.
explanation.definitionFit: A short extract taken from a book or piece of music is a passage.

clue.text: Field occupied by small and large stock

indicators.note: the small letter sits inside the field

parts.note: an arena is a field of activity or contest

explanation.surface: A pitch filled by beasts both small and large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' and 'stock' suggest farming; ARSENAL is a store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons, a stockpile held in reserve.

clue.text: Sources including officer referring to vital town

indicators.note: the sources hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: mines are sources of minerals and ore
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
on means about or concerning
key means vital or crucial

explanation.surface: Insiders cite a junior officer on an important place.
explanation.walkthrough: MILTON KEYNES is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England, built from the late 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: This planned settlement north of London is a large town in Buckinghamshire.
